findings.issue: login() returns { accessToken, user } in the response body while also setting an HttpOnly cookie. The raw JWT is exposed to JavaScript on every login, defeating the purpose of HttpOnly.
findings.suggestion: Remove the accessToken field from the return value. Return only { user } and rely on the cookie for token delivery.

findings.issue: MfaGuard checks req.user.mfaVerified from the JWT payload, but the login endpoint hard-codes mfaVerified: false and no endpoint ever issues a token with mfaVerified: true. ADMIN and FINANCE users are permanently blocked by the guard.
findings.suggestion: Add a POST /mfa/challenge endpoint that accepts a TOTP code, validates it, and returns a new JWT with mfaVerified: true. Until then, do not apply MfaGuard to production routes.

findings.issue: The verification token is sent as a query string parameter on a POST request (?token=...). Query string values appear in server access logs and browser history.
findings.suggestion: Move the token to the POST body: body: JSON.stringify({ token }). Update the controller to read @Body('token') instead of @Query('token').

findings.issue: Session.token is populated at login with a random hex string but is never read by JwtStrategy. It implies a token-binding check that doesn't exist, creating a misleading security signal.
findings.suggestion: Either add a binding check in JwtStrategy (compare the stored token against the cookie value) or remove the column.

findings.issue: User.emailVerificationToken is stored as plaintext. A DB read yields a live verification credential. Password reset tokens are correctly SHA-256 hashed; email tokens should be consistent.
findings.suggestion: Hash the token with crypto.createHash('sha256').update(token).digest('hex') before storing. Re-hash in verifyEmail() before the findUnique lookup.

findings.issue: POST /request-password-reset uses @Body('email') email: string instead of a DTO. The email is never validated for format before reaching usersService.findByEmail().
findings.suggestion: Create a RequestPasswordResetDto with @IsEmail() and use it as the body type.

findings.issue: POST /reset-password has no @Throttle decorator. It inherits the global 10/min default, inconsistent with every other sensitive auth endpoint.
findings.suggestion: Add @Throttle({ default: { limit: 5, ttl: 60000 } }) to the resetPassword handler.

findings.issue: logout, setupMfa, verifyMfa, and validateUser have no test coverage. The MFA enforcement bug (finding #2) would be caught by a verifyMfa test asserting the response JWT contains mfaVerified: true.
findings.suggestion: Add test cases for these four methods before the MFA feature is considered shippable.
